commentsUsed: No feedback logged on the numbers since the last cycle; maxes confirmed still accurate. Trainee requested 3 changes after reviewing the first draft: Conventional Deadlift -> Trap Bar Deadlift, Front Squat -> Back Squat, and Lat Pulldown -> band-assisted Pull-Up (no cable machine; she has pull-up rig access and can do assisted reps). Also fixed vs. the pre-Claude-Code cycle: accessories now actually rotate at the week-2/3 boundary, rotator-cuff work moved to warm-up only (was incorrectly an accessory working set), a rowing and a unilateral-lower movement are now present in every session, GRIP/BALANCE/PLYOMETRIC categories are each covered, and QUAD_DOMINANT now hits its weekly volume target (previously under-programmed).
programName: 4-Week Bone & Muscle Preservation Program — Post-Menopausal Strength (Block 6)
progressionJustification: Continuing DUP from the prior block: it rotates intensity domains (heavy/moderate/volume) across the three weekly sessions, giving superior combined strength and hypertrophy stimulus versus linear progression, which matters for sarcopenia and bone-density work in a post-menopausal trainee. Primary-lift intensities are nudged up ~2% over the prior block given no reported issues completing it. At the trainee's request, Conventional Deadlift was swapped for Trap Bar Deadlift and Front Squat for Back Squat — same categories/volume math, no other changes needed. Lat Pulldown was swapped for band-assisted Pull-Up (no lat pulldown machine available) — bodyweight+band movements don't have a natural %1RM, so this one is progressed by reps/band-assistance level instead and is a documented exception to the "secondary needs percentOfMax" rule. Goblet Squat was added as a new secondary to bring QUAD_DOMINANT up to its weekly target — the prior block only programmed it once. Cable Seated Row was swapped for a Banded Seated Row across all sessions this block — no cable machine available; like the Pull-Up entries above, band-resisted movements don't have a clean %1RM, so this is progressed by reps and band tension instead and is another documented exception to the percentOfMax rule.
weeklyVolumeNotes: GLUTES_HAMSTRINGS (10 sets/week) appears in all 3 sessions via Trap Bar Deadlift primary, Barbell Hip Thrust secondary (S2), and Romanian Deadlift secondary (S3) — the prior block left S2 with no glutes work at all; fixed here. UPPER_BACK_ERECTORS (8/week) via Cable Seated Row (S2) and Chest-Supported DB Row (S3), each bumped to 4 sets to close a gap the prior block left. QUAD_DOMINANT (8/week) now spans 2 sessions — Back Squat primary (S3) plus a new Goblet Squat secondary (S1); the prior block only programmed it once. VERTICAL_PULL is band-assisted Pull-Up (S1, no lat pulldown machine available) — progressed by reps/band-assistance level rather than %1RM since bodyweight+band movements don't have a clean 1RM. UNILATERAL_LOWER (6/leg) via Bulgarian Split Squat/Walking Lunge (S1), DB Step-Up variants (S2), and the explosive step-up (S3, doubles as the plyometric element). CORE (4/week) spread across S1 and S3 only (2 of 3 sessions, meets the spread rule). GRIP and BALANCE each get a dedicated accessory slot in S2 every week; PLYOMETRIC is folded into S3’s step-up. Rowing and a unilateral-lower movement are present in every session. Rotator-cuff activation lives in warm-ups only (not counted as working sets). KNOWN GAPS (see PUSH/VERTICAL_PULL flags): both remain single-session and ~2 sets under target — every other accessory/secondary slot this cycle went to closing gaps left by the prior (unverified) block. Also: hip thrust appears once per week (S2) rather than the rulebook’s 2x/week — traded for actually hitting the GLUTES_HAMSTRINGS 10-12/week target via real secondary-tier volume, which the prior block also failed to do. Flag if you’d rather trade one of the above for the other next cycle.

volumeAudit.flag: Single-session (Landmine Press, S2) and 2 sets under target. Every other secondary/accessory slot this cycle is committed to GLUTES_HAMSTRINGS/GRIP/BALANCE/UNILATERAL_LOWER fixes carried over from the prior block’s gaps — flagging honestly rather than silently shipping it. Next cycle can trade one of those fixes for a second push movement (e.g. DB incline press) if this should take priority.
Single-session (Pull-Up, S1) and 2 sets under target, same root cause as PUSH above — no free secondary/accessory slot remained this cycle to add a second vertical-pull movement.

S3’s exercise is an explosive step-up — tagged UNILATERAL_LOWER (so the app’s own volume audit credits it correctly) but it also satisfies the mandatory low-impact-plyometric element by movement selection.

strength.coachingNotes: New movement (swapped from Cable Seated Row — no cable machine available). Loop a resistance band around your feet while seated with legs extended, or anchor it to a fixed point at chest height. Sit tall, pull to the torso, retract scapulae at the end of the row and hold 1 s, avoid using momentum. Start with a light-medium band, RPE 7-8 for 10 reps.

One-off swap for this session — you did hip thrusts 2 days ago and glutes need a break from that exact pattern. Anchor a band low behind you, walk forward for tension, hinge slightly at the hips and pull the band through between your legs to full hip extension, squeezing glutes hard at the top. Moderate band tension, RPE 7. Hip thrust resumes next session as normal.

Per leg — light-moderate DB, RPE 7-8, hinge at the hip with a soft knee bend, reach toward the floor. Posterior-chain unilateral work, swapped in here to keep Wednesday free of quad loading since Monday and Friday already carry your two weekly squat-pattern quad sessions.
Light DB, forearms on thighs
Eyes open, progress to eyes closed if stable, each side

Low-systemic-fatigue quad isolation finisher, added after Back Squat to build local muscular endurance without compromising Monday's Goblet Squat (only ~48h away). sessions.focus: Weekly Mobility — Shoulder IR, Thoracic Spine, Hips

mobility.name: Sleeper stretch
mobility.notes: Lie on your side, shoulder + elbow at 90°, gently rotate forearm down toward the floor with the OTHER hand — stop at a stretch, not pain. Targets posterior capsule tightness, the usual cause of limited internal rotation.

mobility.name: Thoracic extension over foam roller
mobility.notes: Roller across mid-back, hands behind head, gently extend over it. A lot of apparent shoulder restriction is actually t-spine stiffness.

mobility.name: Shoulder CARs (controlled articular rotations)
mobility.notes: Slow, full-range shoulder circles, standing tall, no weight — you control the range, so this is safe even on a stiff/at-risk shoulder. Stay pain-free.

mobility.name: Couch stretch (hip flexor)
mobility.notes: Back knee down against a couch/wall, brace the glute — offsets the heavy weekly hip-hinge volume.

mobility.name: Cross-body shoulder stretch
mobility.notes: Pull arm across chest with the other hand, posterior capsule.

mobility.name: 90/90 hip switch
mobility.notes: Controlled hip internal/external rotation, both directions.

mobility.name: Calf/ankle wall stretch
mobility.notes: Knee to wall, heel down — ankle dorsiflexion supports squat depth and general fall-risk reduction.

mobility.name: Single-leg balance hold
mobility.notes: Eyes open. Progress toward eyes closed as it gets easy.
